objective: I can practice asking for help clearly. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: When a genuine question or stuck point comes up today, such as an instruction the learner does not understand or a job they cannot finish alone, the learner finds a trusted adult, uses the three-part structure out loud, and the adult confirms afterward whether the request was clear enough to act on right away.
safetyNotes: A trusted adult confirms that the help-asking moment actually happened as described, not only that the learner reports it happened.

simulationAlternative.description: If no real question or stuck point comes up today, the learner instead role-plays the three-part ask-for-help structure with a trusted adult, using a real, specific situation recalled from earlier in the week instead of a live one.

materials: learner-local: a real, current question or stuck point

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u05-l05-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u05-l05-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u05-l05-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u05-l05-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Describe the specific kind of help your adult gave you, such as an explanation, a demonstration, or a decision, and whether it matched what you asked for.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g3-u05-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Clarity of the ask: States all three parts (specific problem, what was already tried, and the kind of help needed) clearly enough for the adult to act without follow-up questions. | Directness: Directly approaches a trusted adult and states the request out loud without prompting. | Transfer to a second instance: The second ask, with a different question, includes all three parts with less reliance on a written reminder. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner use the same three-part structure to ask a co-op teacher or another trusted adult outside the household for help with a different kind of question, showing the structure transfers beyond the household.

duration.elapsedWindow: Two short sessions across one day; no continuous monitoring
duration.sessionPattern: 5 minutes model, 5–7 minutes guided try, 10–15 minutes learner task, 5 minutes evidence and retry check
duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

content: 1. Read the goal for asking for help clearly.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l05-model-card.

resources.title: asking for help clearly coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: When a genuine question or stuck point comes up today, such as an instruction the learner does not understand or a job they cannot finish alone, the learner finds a trusted adult, uses the three-part structure out loud, and the adult confirms afterward whether the request was clear enough to act on right away.
Coach direction: Before asking anyone, think through the three parts of the structure on your own.
Learner prompt: Write the specific problem you have right now, in one sentence.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: asking for help clearly complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Approach a trusted adult and use all three parts of the structure out loud, in order, before pausing for their response.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I named the specific problem, not just a general 'I'm stuck.'
Response 2 (t2-p2): I said what I already tried before asking for help.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I stated exactly what kind of help I needed, such as an explanation, a demonstration, or a decision.
Response 4 (t2-p4): I asked a trusted adult directly, out loud, instead of waiting to be noticed.

Equal-access rule: If no real question or stuck point comes up today, the learner instead role-plays the three-part ask-for-help structure with a trusted adult, using a real, specific situation recalled from earlier in the week instead of a live one.

resources.title: asking for help clearly minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Describe the specific kind of help your adult gave you, such as an explanation, a demonstration, or a decision, and whether it matched what you asked for.

Success checks: Clarity of the ask: States all three parts (specific problem, what was already tried, and the kind of help needed) clearly enough for the adult to act without follow-up questions. | Directness: Directly approaches a trusted adult and states the request out loud without prompting. | Transfer to a second instance: The second ask, with a different question, includes all three parts with less reliance on a written reminder.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: asking for help clearly supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g3-u05-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional asking for help clearly condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Clarity of the ask: States all three parts (specific problem, what was already tried, and the kind of help needed) clearly enough for the adult to act without follow-up questions. | Directness: Directly approaches a trusted adult and states the request out loud without prompting. | Transfer to a second instance: The second ask, with a different question, includes all three parts with less reliance on a written reminder..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

realRoute.title: asking for help clearly — permitted real-life route

steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.

realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record; only the household-authorized guardian attests that the named physical action occurred.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g3-u05-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Clarity of the ask: States all three parts (specific problem, what was already tried, and the kind of help needed) clearly enough for the adult to act without follow-up questions. | Directness: Directly approaches a trusted adult and states the request out loud without prompting. | Transfer to a second instance: The second ask, with a different question, includes all three parts with less reliance on a written reminder.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
